newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom sees second, secured $1 billion Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom sees second, secured $1 billion Eurobond.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly Gazprom will issue a second $1 billion Eurobond, backed by gas exports, the company said in a statement on Friday.
It said the $1 billion secured Eurobond is in addition to an unsecured $1 billion Eurobond and an unsecured $1 billion convertible bond, both of which will be issued this year or in early 1998.

Gazprom, the world's biggest gas producer, said a programme was in place to raise credit, which would include secured and non-secured bonds. It gave no details on when the gas-backed Eurobond was likely to be issued.
It named Dresdner Kleinwort Benson as the consultant on rating the secured Eurobond issue.
Gazprom said a non-secured rating on the company and a rating on the secured Eurobond would be completed after the company published its financial accounts to international standards.
Gazprom has already issued American Depositary Shares, which allow trading of its equity on foreign markets.
